issues.title: Reject malformed explicit plugin contract versions before loading
issues.body:
Outside-merge audit of #848, head `0fb99a0d39ea3b30cab5c4e6fa1ba6a62254937a`, surviving unchanged on dev `aa7d5b6b6dab5cb351991bfbc1b3e92a5ccca12e`.

`API_COMPATIBILITY.md` promises that omitted `contract_version` defaults to version 1, while another value fails discovery before plugin code loads. `validate_plugin_manifest` instead applies `_optional_string(...) or PLUGIN_MANIFEST_CONTRACT_VERSION`; explicit invalid values become the same default as omission.

Independent controls used the existing extension-plugin fixture, valid required manifest fields, actual `discover_plugin_manifests`, and `load_plugin_module`. Omission and string `"1"` are admitted as intended; string `"2"` is rejected. Integer `2`, `null`, `false`, `{}`, `[]`, and `""` are all admitted as version `"1"`, and their plugin module loads. This is a local synthetic contract-boundary result, not evidence that policy, approvals or capability checks were bypassed.

Please distinguish absence from a supplied value in the existing manifest validator: retain the documented omission compatibility, validate supplied versions against the supported contract, and reject unsupported/malformed declarations before module loading. Add focused actual-discovery controls for these values and preserve valid-version and omitted-version neighbors. Reuse the existing error owner; no coercion fallback, extra registry or duplicate validation layer is needed.

Current-dev focused gateway/SDK/plugin tests: 116 passed; critical: 559 passed/4 existing skips; repository Ruff check/format and make lint passed. The existing mismatch test covers only string `"2"`. Refs #848.

issues.body:
Outside-merge audit of #848, head `0fb99a0d39ea3b30cab5c4e6fa1ba6a62254937a`, merge `ab5d1827c7a8bca818774d7a6a83e31205773ea5`. The relevant files survive unchanged on current dev `aa7d5b6b6dab5cb351991bfbc1b3e92a5ccca12e`.

Persisted receipts have no hash-format version or migration. An identical request completed under the previous hash therefore conflicts after upgrading, instead of replaying its retained response.

A newly created current-format receipt replays successfully; changing its body is correctly rejected. The old gateway hash file is byte-identical to the file in the digest-verified official 0.1.24 wheel. This is controlled source/SQLite upgrade evidence, not an observed production incident or an installed-package reproduction; no deleted data or repeated effect was observed.

issues.title: session: SQLiteSessionStore(":memory:").close() leaks temporary storage directory on disk
issues.body:
When instantiating `SQLiteSessionStore(":memory:")` in `src/openminion/modules/session/storage/store.py`, `_build_default_hybrid_store` creates a temporary directory (`tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="openminion-session-store-")`) at lines 163-166 and saves it as `self._temp_root`.

Calling `store.close()` (lines 470-479) closes the SQLite connection and any owned `artifactctl`, but never removes `self._temp_root`. In addition, if initialization fails in `_migrate()`, `_finalize_module_metadata()`, or `_initialize_store_components()` (lines 285-287) after `_init_hybrid_store_and_temp_root()` runs, both `self._temp_root` and `self._record_store` remain open/uncleaned.

Every `:memory:` session store instantiated across test suites or ephemeral runtime checks leaves an `openminion-session-store-*` directory behind on disk.

Minimal repro (verified on `origin/main` `9204d66a`):

```python
from openminion.modules.session.storage.store import SQLiteSessionStore

store = SQLiteSessionStore(":memory:")
temp_root = store._temp_root
print("before close:", temp_root.exists(), temp_root.name.startswith("openminion-session-store-"))
store.close()
print("after close:", temp_root.exists())
```

Output:
```text
before close: True True
after close: True
```

Expected behavior: `store.close()` should remove `self._temp_root` (clearing the reference so repeated `close()` calls are idempotent), and failed `__init__()` attempts after `_init_hybrid_store_and_temp_root()` should run `close()` cleanup before re-raising.

I have a scoped fix and regression tests ready on `princejain756/openminion` (`fix/session-memory-temp-root-cleanup`) if you confirm this is in scope for a PR.

I hit a few coercion bugs in `openminion.modules.brain.diagnostics.status` (`src/openminion/modules/brain/diagnostics/status.py`) while building and testing an app on `openminion==0.1.24` (`a5208844`), and confirmed the same code is still on `dev` (`aa7d5b6b`, Python 3.13.18 on macOS).

Four defects in `status.py`:

1. `coerce_phase_status` fallback crashes on negative token counts (`lines 172-194`): when `PhaseStatus.model_validate(payload)` fails and enters the `except ValidationError:` fallback, it passes `_coerce_int(...)` for `total_input_tokens_used`, `total_output_tokens_used`, and `total_tokens_used` straight into `PhaseStatus(...)` (`ge=0`). Because `_coerce_int` (`lines 304-310`) returns negative integers such as `-1`, the fallback itself raises an uncaught `ValidationError`.
2. `normalize_phase_status` crashes on negative, boolean, or non-finite payload counters (`lines 304-310`, `525-619`): `_coerce_int` allows negative numbers, converts booleans (`True` -> `1`, `False` -> `0`), and does not catch `OverflowError` (for example `float("inf")`). `Agent(output_type=Model)` does not tell the model the schema, so replies fail validation
issues.body:
## Summary
`output_type` only parses the final reply as JSON (`Agent._coerce_output`). The schema is not shown to the model, so a model that is not told the format answers in prose and validation fails.

Environment: OpenMinion 0.1.24, Python 3.14.0, Windows 11, Gemini preset (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`).

## Steps to reproduce
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from openminion import Agent

class Out(BaseModel):
    answer: str

with Agent(instructions="Reply with answer=hello.", output_type=Out) as a:
    a.run("Go.", timeout_seconds=80)
```

## Expected
The model is given `Out`'s JSON schema, or the docs say the schema must be written in `instructions`.

## Actual
`AgentOutputValidationError: Reply did not validate against Out: ... Invalid JSON ... input_value='default: hello'`.
Replies also carry a `default: ` agent-id prefix, so they are never valid JSON on their own and rely on the JSON-extraction fallback.

## Workaround
Put `json.dumps(Out.model_json_schema())` in `instructions` and ask for "ONLY a JSON object". The model still sometimes ends a tool-using turn with prose.

## Suggested fix
Inject the schema into the prompt when `output_type` is a Pydantic model, and strip the `<agent>: ` prefix before parsing. Found while building a project for Cortensor Hackathon #5. Happy to send a PR once the direction is confirmed.

issues.title: `approval_callback` exceptions are swallowed into a normal-looking reply
issues.body:
## Summary
`Agent.run(..., approval_callback=cb)` calls `cb(tool_name, args, approval_id)`. The signature is not in the README or getting-started. If `cb` has a different signature, the resulting `TypeError` is caught by the turn state machine and returned as ordinary reply text instead of being raised.

Environment: OpenMinion 0.1.24, Python 3.14.0, Windows 11, Gemini preset (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`).

## Steps to reproduce
```python
from openminion import Agent, tool

@tool()  # write tool, needs confirmation
def save(text: str) -> str:
    """Pretend to save text."""
    return "saved"

def cb(request):          # 1-arg callback
    return True

with Agent(instructions="Call save with text=hi, then say done.", tools=[save]) as a:
    r = a.run("Go.", approval_callback=cb, timeout_seconds=90)
    print(repr(r.text))
```

## Expected
Either the exception reaches the caller, or the docs show the callback signature `(tool_name: str, args: dict, approval_id: str) -> bool`.

## Actual
No exception. `r.text` is:
`'default: State machine error: RUNTIME_ERROR: cb() takes 1 positional argument but 3 were given'`

## Impact
With `output_type` set, this surfaces as `AgentOutputValidationError` ("Invalid JSON"), which points away from the real cause. It cost several debugging runs.

## Where
`openminion/modules/brain/execution/runtime/turn/dispatch.py`, `_dispatch_runtime_error` turns any exception into `message=f"State machine error: ..."` returned through `_respond_with_meta`.

## Suggested fix
Document the callback signature, and re-raise errors that come from user-supplied callbacks. Found while building a project for Cortensor Hackathon #5. Happy to send a PR once the direction is confirmed.

issues.title: Freshness classifier on small local models misclassifies session-recall turns as live-data requests and forces a canned refusal
issues.body:
**Version / environment**
- openminion 0.1.23 (PyPI), Python 3.12
- Provider: `ollama` (local), model `qwen2.5:1.5b` — the same model serves both the agent and the internal freshness classifier (`modules/brain/bootstrap/freshness_classify.py`)

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Run a multi-turn SDK session in which the agent inspects a local git repository with read-only tools and produces a report.
2. In the same session, ask a pure recall follow-up, e.g.: *"Which project version and latest tag did you find, and what blockers did your report list? Two short sentences."*

**Expected**
The follow-up is classified `local_only` and answered from session context.

**Actual**
The freshness classifier labels the recall question as a live-data request (observed domains: "sports" in one run, "news" in another — non-deterministic), and the runtime forces the canned refusal as the turn's answer:

> "I couldn't provide a grounded current sports answer because Missing live-data evidence for a freshness-sensitive answer.. Please retry with live data available so I can answer with sources and an exact date."

This happens in a session about a local git repository, with no news/sports content anywhere. There appears to be no config option to disable the classifier or pin it to `local_only` for SDK/tool agents.

**Workaround**
Detect the canned refusal verbatim and retry the turn inside the same session; classification is per-turn and non-deterministic, so retries usually pass.

**Impact / suggestion**
On small local models the classifier is effectively random, so ordinary multi-turn SDK workflows intermittently lose turns to a misleading refusal. Suggestions: (a) allow disabling/pinning freshness classification per agent profile, (b) fall back to `local_only` when classifier confidence is low, or (c) don't let a 1-2B-class model make this routing decision unguarded.

issues.title: Localhost provider (ollama) breaks when proxy env vars contain bracketed IPv6 no_proxy entries (Invalid port: ':1]')
issues.body:
**Version / environment**
- openminion 0.1.23 (PyPI), Python 3.12, Linux VM (sandboxed CI-style environment)
- Provider: `ollama` (local), model `qwen2.5:1.5b`, base URL `http://127.0.0.1:11434`
- Environment has `http_proxy` / `https_proxy` / `all_proxy` set to an HTTP egress proxy, and `no_proxy` / `NO_PROXY` containing bracketed IPv6 entries, e.g. `localhost,127.0.0.1,::1,[::1],...`

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Configure a project-scoped config with the `ollama` provider (`openminion config init --provider ollama`).
2. With the proxy variables above present in the environment, run `openminion doctor --check-turn`.

**Expected**
The turn smoke test reaches the local Ollama server on `127.0.0.1:11434` (localhost traffic should not be affected by proxy settings, and bracketed `no_proxy` entries are common in sandboxed environments).

**Actual**
```
[FAIL] agent.turn_smoke: Agent turn smoke test failed: PROVIDER_ERROR: The configured model provider failed before it could return a decision (InvalidURL: Invalid port: ':1]'). Please retry or switch models.
```
The failing fragment `:1]` is the tail of the bracketed entry `[::1]`, which suggests the proxy / no-proxy parsing mishandles bracketed IPv6 entries even though the target URL is plain IPv4 localhost.

**Workaround**
Unsetting `http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `all_proxy`, `no_proxy` (and uppercase variants) for the OpenMinion process makes the smoke test pass immediately.

**Impact**
Anyone running OpenMinion with a local provider inside a corporate/CI/sandbox network with proxy env vars gets a cryptic failure on the very first turn, with no hint that proxies are involved.

issues.title: session: diff_session_branches hashes session_id/timestamps into refs and carry_forward_branch_fields drops summary refs
issues.body:
### Summary

`diff_session_branches` and `carry_forward_branch_fields` (`src/openminion/modules/session/fork_restore/branch.py`, exposed via `sessctl branch-diff` and `sessctl branch-carry-forward` in `src/openminion/modules/session/cli.py`) exhibit three concrete structural-diff and carry-forward defects:

1. **`diff_session_branches` hashes per-session identity and row metadata into `summary` and `working_state` refs via `_stable_ref` (`branch.py:128-146`)**:
   - `_diff_summary` hashes `{"text": store.get_summary(sid), "refs": store.get_summaries(sid)}` with `_stable_ref`. `SummaryStore.get_summaries(sid)` always returns `{"session_id": sid, "base_ref": ..., "delta_refs": [...], "delta_items": [...]}` (including `"session_id"` and per-delta `"ts"`), and the outer dict is never empty. As a result, for any two distinct sessions (`left != right`):
     - Two brand-new empty sessions report `summary: status="changed"` (`left_ref != "empty"`, `left_ref != right_ref`) instead of `status="same"` (`"empty"`).
     - One summarized session vs one empty session reports `summary: status="changed"` instead of `"added_or_removed"`.
     - Two sessions with identical summaries (including `source` vs the child just created by `carry_forward_branch_fields`), or differing only in `summary_long`, report wrong `summary` status.
   - `_diff_working_state` hashes `store.get_latest_working_state(sid) or {}` via `_stable_ref`, which includes `"session_id"`, `"version"`, and `"ts"` (`StateStore.get_latest_working_state`), so two distinct sessions with identical `state_ref` and `state_inline` always report `working_state: status="changed"` instead of `"same"`.
2. **`_carry_summary` and `_carry_working_state` drop or alter structural fields (`branch.py:167-187`)**:
   - `_carry_summary` reads `summaries = store.get_summaries(source)` without copying `base_ref` (`set_summary_base`) or `delta_refs` (`append_summary_delta`), so summary base/delta references are lost on carry-forward (and sessions holding only `base_ref`/`delta_refs` copy nothing), while child summary refresh semantics require keeping the child's local `based_on_seq=0` cursor rather than copying the source event sequence

`RepoMapCache` (`src/openminion/modules/context/repo_map/cache.py`, consumed by `build_repo_map_section(..., cache=...)` in `src/openminion/modules/context/repo_map/section.py`) drops all symbols from Python files in subdirectories during `refresh()` and drops all symbols from unchanged files after `save_to()` / `load_from()`:

### Summary

`purge_soft_deleted` (`src/openminion/modules/memory/runtime/purge.py`, invoked by `run_gc` and `memctl gc`) still selects expired records using raw lexicographic string comparison (`expires_at < ?` in `_sqlite_purgeable_ids` at `purge.py:212` and `expires_at < :now` in `_postgres_purgeable_rows` at `purge.py:80`) against `utc_now().isoformat()` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff+00:00`), instead of the instant predicates established for active retrieval in `storage/sqlite/queries.py::expiry_clause` and `storage/postgres/queries.py::_EXPIRY_CLAUSE` (#683 / #677):

1. **Future offset-bearing expiries are permanently hard-deleted**: A live record whose `expires_at` is hours in the future in a negative UTC offset (e.g. `2026-11-20T14:20:00-12:00` when UTC `now` is `2026-11-20T22:20:00+00:00`) is readable through `list`, `search`, and `retrieve_by_entities`, yet `"2026-11-20T14:20:00-12:00" < "2026-11-20T22:20:00+00:00"` evaluates to `True`, permanently deleting the record, its FTS/entity/relation/tier-transition rows, and its artifact reference edges.

issues.title: SSM transport can leave dispatched attempts unfinished or mark failed/missing-code invocations succeeded
issues.body:
### Summary

`SsmTransport.run` (`src/openminion/tools/ops/transports/ssm.py`) mishandles malformed synthetic payloads as well as contradictory or unobserved terminal AWS SSM `GetCommandInvocation` responses across four boundaries, either inventing observed outcomes or letting `KeyError`/`TypeError` escape `OpsService.submit` and `OpsService._dispatch_plan` (which catch `(OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError)` and otherwise leave a dispatched plan attempt unfinished with `status="running"`, `attempt_phase="dispatch_intent"`):

1. **Missing, synthetic `None`, boolean, or non-integer `ResponseCode` on terminal invocations (`ssm.py:131-133`)**:
   - In AWS SSM [`GetCommandInvocation`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/APIReference/API_GetCommandInvocation.html), `Status` (`Pending | InProgress | Delayed | Success | Cancelled | TimedOut | Failed | Cancelling`) is documented separately from `StatusDetails` (`Delivery Timed Out`, `Execution Timed Out`, `Undeliverable`, `Terminated`, etc.), and `ResponseCode` is an integer (`-1` when the command has not been started or the command result was not received).
   - On synthetic/malformed payloads where `"ResponseCode"` is omitted on `Status="Success"`, `invocation.get("ResponseCode", 0)` invents a zero exit code without an observed return code, while `"ResponseCode": False` coerces to `0` (`bool` subclasses `int`).
   - On synthetic/malformed payloads where `"ResponseCode"` is `None` (or non-numeric), `invocation.get("ResponseCode", ...)` returns `None` and `int(None)` raises uncaught `TypeError`, leaving an active `OpsService` plan attempt unfinished.
2. **Contradictory or unobserved terminal `Status` / `ResponseCode` combinations (`ssm.py:129-140`, `service.py:266-268, 534-536`)**:
   - When `Status="Failed"` is paired with `ResponseCode=0`, `SsmTransport.run` returns `TransportResult(return_code=0, cancelled=False, timed_out=False)`, causing `build_evidence` and `OpsService._finish_plan_result` to record `claim_status="observed"`, `remote_outcome="exit_observed"`, and `status="succeeded"` (and rewriting `ResponseCode=0` to `1` would fabricate an invented exit code under `remote_outcome="exit_observed"`).

issues.title: tool: add file.mkdir and file.copy to the file family
issues.body:
**Gap.** The file family ships `file.list_dir`, `file.read`, `file.read_range`, `file.write`, `file.find`, `file.search`, `file.edit` and `file.trash`. There is no tool that creates a directory, and none that copies a file. Workspace setup therefore needs `file.write` to a path whose parents it happens to create, or `exec.run`, and copying a file means reading it and writing the contents back through the model.

**Proposal, one bounded slice.**

- `file.mkdir(path, parents=false)`, creates one directory; with `parents` it creates missing parents. Returns `created: true` when it created the directory and `false` when the directory already exists. A non-directory at the path is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, a missing parent without `parents` is `NOT_FOUND`.
- `file.copy(source, destination, overwrite=false)`, copies one file's contents to `destination`, creating its parent directories as `file.write` already does; an existing destination without `overwrite` is `PRECONDITION_FAILED`; a directory as source or destination is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Returns `bytes` copied.

Both are `WRITE_SAFE`, blocked under read-only mode, resolved through the existing `resolve_path` containment (`source` as a read, `destination` as a write), and rejected by the memory backend with an explicit reason the way `file.trash` is. Both resolve through the shared path policy before the backend, so a symlinked source is followed to its target; there is no separate symlink policy here, only the existing containment. No recursive directory copy, no metadata preservation, no overwrite-by-default: those are separate decisions.

**Why this shape.** `file.write` already creates parent directories, so `mkdir` exists for the case it cannot express, an empty directory or a tree with no file to write. `file.copy` is the same kind of wrapper and keeps bytes on the machine instead of round-tripping content through the model.

**Validation plan.** Handler controls for create/exists/wrong-type/missing-parent, copy/refuse-existing/overwrite/directory-neighbour/parent-creation, the memory-backend rejection, and the registrar manifest listing both tools; plus the existing file and coding-mode suites, which must stay unc

issues.title: Agent(instructions=...) longer than ~860 characters is truncated silently; later rules never reach the model
issues.body:
### Summary

Text passed as `Agent(instructions=...)` is rendered into the `[IDENTITY]` block of the system prompt and capped by the context
budget `identity_tokens` (160 for `decide`, 180-220 for other purposes in `modules/context/schemas/budgets.py`). Anything past the
cap is cut and replaced by `...[truncated]`. Nothing is logged to the SDK caller or returned in `AgentRunResult`, so rules placed at the
end of the instructions (output format, "never do X") silently stop working.

### Reproduce

Self-contained, no model needed (a 20-line local OpenAI-compatible endpoint records the request):

```bash
python findings/capture_server.py /tmp/req.jsonl &
export OPENMINION_HOME=$(mktemp -d) OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY=dummy
openminion setup --provider custom-openai-compatible --model capture --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18099/v1 --no-chat
python findings/f3_instructions_truncated.py /tmp/req.jsonl
```

(Files: https://github.com/swiftbotlabs/repro-scribe/tree/main/findings)

### Expected

All 40 numbered rules (2,159 characters) reach the model, or the SDK warns that the instructions were shortened.

### Actual

```
instructions: 2159 chars, 40 rules; the last rule that reached the model: 16
```

The identity block in the captured request ends with `...[truncated]` after rule 16.

### Environment

openminion 0.1.23 (a55a98a), Python 3.14.4, Linux aarch64; provider-independent (seen with Gemini and with the capture endpoint).

### Suggested fix

1. When SDK-provided instructions exceed the identity budget, emit a warning (log + `AgentRunResult.metadata["instructions_truncated"]`
   with the kept/total characters).
2. Document the limit next to `instructions=` in the SDK docs and examples.
3. Optionally let `Agent(...)` raise the identity budget for caller instructions (e.g. `instructions_budget_tokens=`), since SDK
   instructions are the caller's contract, not optional persona text.

We are happy to send a PR for (1) and (2) once you confirm the direction.

issues.body:
**Affected version:** openminion 0.1.23, Ollama provider, llama3.1:8b

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Run an agent turn that performs tool work in a session (e.g. records triage decisions via tools).
2. In the same session, ask a recall question about that work: "From your triage in this session: which issue ids are release blockers, and what version are the release notes for? Answer briefly."
3. Observe the reply.

**Expected behavior**
The question is about the session's own local state — not about current external facts — so it should be answered from session context without a freshness classification.

**Actual behavior**
Reply: *"I couldn't provide a grounded current regulation answer because Missing live-data evidence for a freshness-sensitive answer.. Please retry with live data available so I can answer with sources and an exact date."* The run metadata shows a `freshness_classify` LLM call; the question was classified freshness-sensitive and the turn refused. (The message also says "regulation", which has nothing to do with the task.)

**Impact**
Multi-turn agents that report back on their own work — a basic pattern for release/QA assistants — lose their second turn to a false-positive guardrail, with a confusing message.

Verified run transcript from our Cortensor Hackathon #5 project (ReleasePilot), turn 2 of the end-to-end run.

issues.title: Echo (demo) provider silently produces "successful" runs that never call tools
issues.body:
**Affected version:** openminion 0.1.23 (source checkout, Python 3.12, Linux)

**Steps to reproduce**
1. `openminion config init --provider echo`
2. Run `examples/sdk/tool_agent.py` (or any `Agent(tools=[...], forced_tools=[...])` program) against the echo-configured default agent.
3. Observe the run completes successfully and prints the prompt text back.

**Expected behavior**
Either the echo provider should honour `forced_tools` with a synthetic tool call (so tool plumbing can be smoke-tested offline), or `Agent.run()` / `openminion doctor` should surface a clear warning that the configured provider cannot call tools and the run exercised no tool code paths.

**Actual behavior**
The run returns `run_state` success with the user prompt echoed as the reply (`openminion: <prompt>`). No tool is invoked — including explicitly forced tools — and nothing in the result metadata flags that zero tool calls happened. A builder following the SDK examples can believe their tool agent works when it has never executed a tool.

**Impact**
Hackathon/CI smoke tests built on the documented offline provider can pass vacuously. This cost us one debugging cycle while building a Cortensor Hackathon #5 entry (ReleasePilot, a repo release assistant): our tools were only proven once we switched to a real local model (Ollama).

**Evidence**
- Run transcript from our project (echo run, both turns echo the prompt, no tool calls in metadata).
- Echo adapter source: `src/openminion/modules/llm/providers/echo/adapter.py` always returns `tool_calls=[]`.

**Suggested fix**
In the runtime, when a run ends with tools registered (or forced) but zero tool calls and the provider is `echo`, add a `warnings` entry to the run result metadata, e.g. `provider_echo_no_tool_calls`.

issues.body:
**Idea.** A seamless capture trigger so a screenshot can go into a turn without a detour through a file: a global hotkey and/or reading recent image payloads from the system clipboard, across Desktop and the CLI/Focus.

**What the framework already owns.** Selected images exist end to end: `openminion run --image`, Focus `/image add`, `/image mode`, `turns.images.v1`, and the artifact ingestion behind `read_selected_images` (`cli/transport/images.py`) with its bounds — at most four images, 10 MiB each, 20 MiB per request, PNG/JPEG/WebP only, decode bounded to 20 megapixels. `docs/selected-images.md` documents the contract, and the Desktop app already consumes the same runtime surface (`POST /v1/sessions/<id>/images` plus `image_refs` on the turn).

**Research findings, so the scope is honest.**

1. *A global hotkey cannot be implemented in the CLI.* A foreground terminal process receives no global key events; the terminal emulator or the OS owns them first. The hotkey half is therefore that repository's change.

issues.body:
The prompt-facing tool result is capped at a fixed 1200 characters, and the operator knob that looks like it controls
that cap does not. A large tool output reaches the model as 0.37% of itself with no way to tell how much was dropped.

## Environment

- Arch Linux, kernel `7.2.11-arch1-1`, x86_64
- system Python `3.14.9`; project venv Python **3.11.16** (the interpreter everything below ran under)
- openminion `dev` at `83e535fff814ccb0771a1ea8ca50710023b24a7e`, read-only source checkout with `PYTHONPATH=src` (no
  install into the shared venv, per the testing doc's worktree rule)
- no daemon, no provider calls: the measurements are direct calls into the real owners

## Prerequisites (from the repo docs)

`docs/testing-and-validation.md` "Install baseline": Python 3.11 or newer; a recent `pip` supporting PEP 660 editable
installs; `python3.11 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && make dev-install`. A worktree may reuse another
environment read-only via `PYTHONPATH=src`, but must not install into it.

`docs/getting-started.md` "Fast bootstrap": the same venv + `make dev-install` + `make hooks-install`, or
`pipx install openminion` / `uv tool install openminion` for ordinary use.

## Measured

Constructed real `ActionResult`s and rendered them with the real converter
(`modules/brain/loop/tools/messages.action_result_to_tool_message`):

| input | raw | what the model sees | retained |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000-line stdout (~60 chars/line) | 359,999 chars | 1,319 chars, cut mid-line, trailing `...[truncated]` | **0.37%** |
| 5,000-item list in `outputs` | 5,000 items | 16 items + `...[4984 more item(s)]` | 0.3% |
| nested value at depth 9 | — | `"[truncated]"` at the depth limit | — |

The boundary event emitted at the same seam (`_pidf_emit_boundary_event("tool_output", body, …)`) carries the
**truncated** body, and neither the message nor the event carries the original length — `str(359999)` does not appear in
either.

issues.body:
The freshness classifier is skipped whenever a message opens with a verb plus a tool-shaped noun, and the skip leaves the
turn with the neutral freshness contract — so a genuinely time-sensitive request can bypass freshness checking entirely.

## Mechanism

`modules/brain/bootstrap/freshness_classify.py`:

- `_DIRECT_TOOL_VERB_RE` (`:36-39`) matches `^(please )?(use|run|call|invoke) (the )?<token>`.
- `_direct_tool_request_name` (`:42-52`) returns that token normalised to a tool name, or the `tool <name>` form.
- On a match, classification is skipped (`classifier_mode = "skipped_direct_tool_request"`) and the contract becomes
  `FreshnessContract(intent=<tool>)` — no model call at all.

## Measured behaviour (dev `84b2b27e`, real matcher)

| message | returns | classifier |
|---|---|---|
| `use the time tool to get now` | `time` | skipped (intended) |
| `tool time now` | `time` | skipped (intended) |
| `run time estimates for the crawl` | **`time`** | **skipped (false positive)** |
| `call time on this project` | **`time`** | **skipped (false positive)** |
| `invoke search to find the docs` | `None` | runs ('search' is not a registered tool name) |
| `what time is it right now` | `None` | runs |
| `use the wall clock please` | `None` | runs |
| `please don't use the time tool` | `None` | runs (anchored at start) |

`require_live_data=False, require_sources=False, require_exact_date=False, require_explicit_failure_wording=False,
answer_mode=local_only` — byte-identical to the neutral empty contract. So the false-positive cases do not merely skip a
classification, they proceed with **no freshness obligation at all** while the request plausibly needs live data.

Accept the skip only for the explicit, unambiguous `tool <name>` form, and only when `<name>` is an exactly registered
visible tool. For the verb form, either drop it or require the matched token to be an exact registered tool name **and**
not a common noun that also appears in ordinary prose — which is hard to do by regex, so dropping it is the honest

issues.body:
The per-loop read cache can keep serving results after the underlying file changed, because invalidation only recognises a
narrow write shape. Measured on dev `84b2b27e` against the real `LoopCache`.

## Mechanism

`modules/brain/loop/tools/cache.py`: a per-loop cache for read tools
(`file.read`, `file.read_range`, `code.grep`, `file.list_dir`, `file.find`, `file_read`) keyed by
`sha256({"tool": name, "args": args})` with `sort_keys=True` and `default=str`. Only successful, non-job results are
stored. `invalidate_for_write` removes entries whose recorded paths intersect the write's paths, and only for
`_WRITE_TOOLS` (`file.write`, `code.patch`, `file.edit`, `file.trash`, `file_write`), where paths are taken from the keys
`path`, `file`, `directory`, `target`.

## Measured gaps

Unit probe against the real class, one loop instance:

| sequence | result |
|---|---|
| `file.read a.py` → `file.write {"path": "a.py"}` | cache entry removed (positive control) |
| `code.grep {"pattern": "needle"}` → `file.write {"path": "a.py"}` | **grep result still served** |
| `file.read c.py` → `exec.run {"cmd": "echo x > c.py"}` | **read still served** |
| `file.read d.py` → `file.write {"filename": "d.py"}` | **read still served** |

Three distinct causes: a read tool whose args carry no path (grep, find) records an empty path set and can never be
invalidated; a write tool outside `_WRITE_TOOLS` (shell/exec, MCP tools, artifact writers) never triggers invalidation
at all; and a write whose path argument uses another name records nothing.

Within one adaptive loop the model sees cached tool output as trusted state. A stale read means it can reason about, and
act on, file content that no longer exists — and the loop has no TTL, no mtime or size check, and no way for the caller
to know a hit is old. The cache is per-loop and the loop executes its batches on one thread (no `ThreadPool` in the tools
engine), so there is no concurrent-writer race today; the correctness risk is invalidation coverage, not locking.

1. **Generation counter (recommended).** Any write-capable tool bumps a generation; cached read results carry the

issues.body:
`config import --force` replaces the stored config with nothing to inspect first. The only way to see what
a candidate file will do is to import it and compare afterwards, and doing that by hand is exactly when
credentials leak into a diff.

## Proposal

`openminion config diff <file>`: build the config that `config import <file>` would produce and print the
leaf-level differences, without writing anything.

- merge by default (what `config import` does), `--replace` to mirror `config import --force`
- output: per-leaf `added` / `removed` / `changed` paths with before/after values, or `--json`
- exit `0` when the stored config would be unchanged, `1` when it would differ, `2` through the existing
  typed-error boundary for an unreadable candidate
- secret leaves excluded from the comparison and from output, using the same sanitizer `config export`
  already applies
- no write in any case

## Reuse, not new surface

Active side loads through the same `load_cli_config` that `config show` uses; the candidate goes through the
existing `load_config_import` (so the diff is the import's own merge semantics, not a re-implementation);
secrets are stripped with the existing `_strip_secrets_in_place`. One new subparser, one leaf-walk helper.
No new config keys, no daemon call, no new state, no change to `config import` behaviour, and no new
provider or storage surface.

## Controls

1. identical candidate -> "No changes", exit 0
2. one changed leaf -> reported with both values, exit 1
3. `--json` payload: `active`, `candidate`, `mode`, `secrets_excluded`, `changed`, `changes`
4. `--replace` reports removals that merge mode keeps
5. a changed secret value never appears in text or JSON output
6. missing candidate file -> typed error, no write
7. empty argument -> typed error, no write

`POST /v1/sessions/<id>/turn-inputs` with `intent=steer_current` against a **live** turn returns

before the next steering hook, that entry is never applied, never marked deferred, never consumed by
a later turn and never expired — it stays `queued` with no automatic retirement. Because queued entries count against
`max_pending_per_session` (20), repeating it makes the session refuse **all** turn inputs with

- The only consumer of a targeted steer is `apply_turn_steering`

  `target_trace_id`), and it is called only at loop iteration boundaries:
  `modules/brain/loop/tools/budget_control.py:597`, `:898`;
  `modules/brain/loop/tools/postprocess/engine.py:242`, `:544`;
  `modules/brain/loop/tools/budget_finalization.py:180`;
  `modules/brain/loop/tools/duplicate_batch.py:523`. A turn whose last provider reply ends it never

issues.body:
## Summary

`openminion mcp import --from <path>` reads the source file without validating it, so the two most
likely user mistakes — a path that does not exist and a file that is not valid JSON — escape the
command and are caught by the CLI's terminal boundary, which classifies them as `internal error`
and tells the user to re-run with `--verbosity verbose` for a traceback. Both are input errors,
and two sibling commands that read a user-supplied path already return a specific, structured
failure instead.

## Cause

`src/openminion/cli/commands/mcp.py:236-241` (`_mcp_import`):

```python
source_path = Path(str(getattr(args, "source", "") or "")).expanduser()
payload = json.loads(source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
```

There is no existence check and no parse guard, so `FileNotFoundError` / `json.JSONDecodeError`
propagate. The terminal boundary in `src/openminion/cli/main.py` is a curated tuple of failure
families (including `OSError`), so these land in its `internal error: <Type>: <msg>` branch — a
classification meant for unexpected failures, not for a bad argument value. The success path
(`mcp.py:254-262`) already prints a JSON payload `{"ok": true, "imported": [...], "written": ...}`,
so the command has a structured result shape to fail in.

Contrast, same class of input, same head:

| command | rc | output |

| `mcp import --from <file containing {"mcpServers": {>` | 1 | `openminion: internal error: JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 17 (char 16)` |
| `skill ingest --file /nonexistent/SKILL.md` | 1 | `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "PATH_NOT_FOUND", "message": "File does not exist", "details": {"path": "/nonexistent/SKILL.md"}}}` |

issues.title: cli: bare `openminion replay` crashes with AttributeError instead of usage
issues.body:
## Summary

A bare `openminion replay` (group name, no subcommand) dispatches into the group handler with no
subcommand selected and crashes with an uncaught `AttributeError` traceback at `rc=1`. Sibling
groups and the group's own subcommands reject the same invocation with `rc=2` and a usage line.

## Cause

- `src/openminion/cli/commands/replay.py:163` registers the group's subcommands with
  `parser.add_subparsers(dest="replay_command")` and no `required=True`, so argparse happily parses
  `replay` with `replay_command` unset.
- The handler is then invoked anyway: `src/openminion/cli/commands/replay.py:27` reads
  `args.task_db`, an attribute only the subcommand parsers define, so the call raises
  `AttributeError: 'Namespace' object has no attribute 'task_db'`.
- The CLI's terminal boundary (`src/openminion/cli/main.py:312` dispatch, boundary catches
  `(ConfigError, RuntimeError, KeyError)` plus the curated failure families) deliberately lets
  `AttributeError` through as a programming error, so the user sees a traceback rather than usage.

Groups that already do this correctly reject the bare form in the parser: `sessions`, `memory`,
`channel`, `mcp`, `identity`, `status`, `service` all exit 2 with a usage line, and
`replay checkpoints` (with its required arguments missing) does too.

## Reproduction

```bash
SRC=/path/to/openminion                   # source checkout at dev
PY=/path/to/venv/bin/python
export HOME=/tmp/om-replay/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/om-replay/home/.config PYTHONPATH=$SRC
mkdir -p /tmp/om-replay/home /tmp/om-replay/work && cd /tmp/om-replay/work
$PY -m openminion config init --provider echo

$PY -m openminion replay; echo "rc=$?"
$PY -m openminion replay --help; echo "rc=$?"     # lists checkpoints/replay/compare/rewind/branch
$PY -m openminion replay checkpoints; echo "rc=$?"  # rc=2 + usage: required args
```

issues.title: cli: `openminion time <subcommand>` fails with tool_not_found on the default daemon route
issues.body:
## Summary

`openminion time <subcommand>` fails on the default runtime route with `tool_not_found`. The
`time` group dispatches per-action tool names (`time.now`, `time.in_zone`, ...), but the HTTP
tool route resolves those names against the model-facing tool inventory, which exposes a single
aggregated `time` tool. The same command succeeds with `runtime.process_mode = "single-process"`,
so the group is unusable on a default install (the daemon route is the default).

## Cause

- `src/openminion/cli/commands/time.py:16-27` maps every subcommand to a per-action tool name and
  `_dispatch` (`time.py:34-40`) sets `proxy.tool = tool_name`, so with the daemon runtime the CLI
  sends `POST /v1/tools/time.now/run`.
- `src/openminion/api/routes/tools.py:203` resolves that name with `v1_tool_schema`
  (`api/core/deps.py:73`) -> `api/queries/runtime_reports.py:64-67`, which matches only names
  present in `build_tool_inventory_report`. That report exposes one `time` entry, so the lookup
  returns `None`, and the route answers 404 `tool_not_found` before executing anything.
- The per-action specs themselves do exist (`src/openminion/tools/time/plugin.py:741+` registers
  `name="time.now"`, `"time.in_zone"`, ...), and the in-process CLI path resolves them: the same
  command returns `ok: true` with `runtime_source: inproc`.

So the gap is between the name the CLI dispatches and the name set the HTTP tool route accepts;
it is not a missing tool implementation.

## Reproduction

```bash
SRC=/path/to/openminion                   # source checkout at dev
PY=/path/to/venv/bin/python
export HOME=/tmp/om-probe/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/om-probe/home/.config PYTHONPATH=$SRC
mkdir -p /tmp/om-probe/home /tmp/om-probe/work && cd /tmp/om-probe/work

$PY -m openminion config init --provider echo
$PY -m openminion daemon start            # default route

$PY -m openminion time now; echo "rc=$?"
$PY -m openminion time in-zone --timezone Europe/Helsinki; echo "rc=$?"

# what the same route exposes
$PY -m openminion tools list | grep -o '"name": "[^"]*"' | grep -c '"name": "time"'     # 1
